EventFlow Privacy Policy

Last updated: November 4, 2026

This Privacy Policy describes how Everlight Digital ("we", "us") handles information when you use EventFlow ("EventFlow").

The Everlight Digital Privacy Policy applies generally to EventFlow. The EventFlow-specific data handling section below describes what EventFlow collects, where that information is kept, and who else receives it.

EventFlow-specific data handling

EventFlow is a web app we run for churches and nonprofits that coordinate volunteer events. You use it in a browser, including as an installable web app. We also offer an API and, if someone in your organization allows it, a connection so an assistant can read and update events on that person's behalf. We do not offer a separate mobile app, and we do not take payments.

What we collect. When you join, we store your name, email address, and a hashed password if you set one. Some volunteers join from a public sign-up link with a name and email and no password, and sign in later from a link we email them. We store your role, which ministries you belong to, your email notification settings, your time zone, and the last time you used the app. We do not store your IP address in our database. We use the IP address only in server memory, for a short time, to limit repeated login and email requests.

For each event your organization enters, we store the details your team types: title, dates and times, location, description, ministry, audience, and the owner's name, email, and phone when those are provided. We store tasks, who they are assigned to, whether each person accepted, notes, comments, and checklist items. We store the dates you mark yourself unavailable, and an optional note with those dates. On the day of an event we can record that you checked in. After an event we store the debrief your team writes, a headcount, a volunteer count, and a cost if someone enters them. We do not keep a list of individual attendees. If your organization connects Planning Center, we store the attendance total we read from it, not the check-in roster.

Messages you send in a channel or a direct message, and files you upload (images and PDFs up to 25 MB, plus the original file name), are stored for your organization. A public sign-up page shows the organization's name, the event, the date, and the open jobs to anyone who has the link, and asks that person for a name and email.

Where we keep it. Account, event, task, message, and debrief data are in a Postgres database hosted with our application on Railway. Uploaded files are stored on a disk volume attached to that same service. We do not state a data-center region in the application configuration. We serve the site over HTTPS. The application itself sets a rule that browsers should use HTTPS for a year, and the sign-in cookie is marked secure in production.

Who else receives it. We send email through Resend. Those messages include your email address and the content of the notice, such as your name, task and event titles, your organization's name, and links to accept a task, reset a password, or sign in. You can turn categories of those messages off, and each message includes an unsubscribe link. Your browser loads the Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts from Google Fonts, which receives the usual connection data for that request and does not receive your EventFlow account. If an administrator connects Planning Center, we send that organization's Planning Center access token to Planning Center and read event names and attendance totals. If our optional LifeOS connection is turned on for a single configured account, that account's upcoming event names and open task titles are sent to that service. We do not send your data to an AI provider ourselves. If you allow an assistant to connect, that assistant receives the events, tasks, people (name, email, and role), and workload information covered by the access you approve. Access lasts about an hour and can be refreshed for up to 30 days, until you revoke it in Settings. An hourly job run by GitHub Actions receives only summary counts of what the mail job did, not message contents. We do not use an analytics or error-tracking service, and we do not use a payment processor.

Cookies and on your device. We set one sign-in cookie, named token. It is httpOnly, sent only to our site, and in production only over HTTPS. It holds a signed session for your user id, organization, and role, and the server stops accepting it after 7 days. We do not set an expiration date on the cookie itself, so your browser keeps it for the browsing session. Signing out clears it. We store a few display preferences in your browser's local storage, such as whether a list is filtered to your own events. The installed web app can keep up to 100 recent API responses on your device for up to 24 hours so pages can load when the network is slow. Those cached responses can include information your account is allowed to see.

How long we keep it. We keep organization data until someone in the organization deletes the record, or until the organization is removed from the database. The app does not include a control that deletes a user account or an entire organization. Claimed copies of outbound email are removed from our queue after 30 days. Sign-in links expire after 15 minutes and password-reset links after 60 minutes. Invites expire after 14 days. Deleting a message hides it and stops its attachments from being downloaded. The message text remains in the database, and the attachment file remains on disk. Deleting a single uploaded graphic removes that file. Deleting an event removes it and its tasks, comments, and related rows from the database. Files that were uploaded to that event can remain on the disk volume. We do not collect a date of birth or an age. If your team writes pastoral or other sensitive notes into an event, a task, a debrief, or a message, we store that text the same way we store any other text in those fields.
